findings.highlight: the burning hallway
findings.evidenceJa: ごうごうともえるロウカ
findings.governingReading: the hallway burning with a roar
findings.explanation: The English omits the overwhelming fire sound from the child’s memory.

findings.highlight: I should be fine by myself
findings.evidenceJa: ひとりでいけるな
findings.governingReading: you can go on alone, right
findings.explanation: The father’s instruction about the child moving alone becomes a general reassurance about independence.

findings.highlight: told me to wait here
findings.evidenceJa: 外でまっていなさい
findings.governingReading: told him to wait outside
findings.explanation: The English removes the destination that sends the child out of the burning house.

findings.highlight: I finally confronted the scene
findings.evidenceJa: 初めて、その光景と正面から対峙した
findings.governingReading: for the first time, he confronted that scene head-on
findings.explanation: “Finally” replaces the first occurrence and the direct face-to-face quality disappears.

findings.highlight: an event that cannot be redone
findings.evidenceJa: 変えられない出来事だ
findings.governingReading: an event that cannot be changed
findings.explanation: The English shifts irreversible reality into inability to repeat or redo the event.

findings.highlight: the presence of death wanting to take me
findings.evidenceJa: 生きている俺を仲間にしたがる死の気配
findings.governingReading: the presence of death wanting to make the living child one of its companions
findings.explanation: mirror moon removes the child’s image of death recruiting him into the dead.

findings.highlight: my brain was being steamed inside my skull. steamed.
findings.evidenceJa: 脳みそは頭の中で蒸し焼きだ
findings.governingReading: his brain is being steam-roasted inside his head
findings.explanation: A stray repeated “steamed” corrupts the sentence, and steam-roasting is weakened to steaming.

findings.highlight: It passed the boiling point to reach the freezing point
findings.evidenceJa: 沸点を超えたらぐるりと回って凍結温度
findings.governingReading: past boiling, temperature circles all the way around to freezing
findings.explanation: The surreal full-circle inversion is reduced to linear passage between temperatures.

findings.highlight: burning up and dying seemed like a human death
findings.evidenceJa: やけしぬのはニンゲンらしくてただしいとおもった
findings.governingReading: he thought burning to death was humanlike and therefore right or proper
findings.explanation: The English preserves human death but omits the child’s horrifying judgment that it is the correct alternative.

findings.highlight: I found out that it was going to rain soon
findings.evidenceJa: いずれ雨が降ると知って
findings.governingReading: knowing that rain would fall eventually
findings.explanation: Existing knowledge and indefinite futurity become a new discovery that rain is imminent.

findings.highlight: My temples feel hot
findings.evidenceJa: 額に熱さを感じながら
findings.governingReading: feeling heat in his forehead
findings.explanation: The location of Shirou’s fever sensation shifts to both temples.

findings.highlight: Why did my dream contain as far as the smell of the burning air
findings.evidenceJa: 爆ぜる空気の匂いまで実感するような夢
findings.governingReading: a dream vivid enough to feel even the smell of bursting, burning air
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and weakens the exploding air to merely burning air.

findings.highlight: The breaker in my body trips, telling me not to think about it
findings.evidenceJa: 体についたブレイカーが落ちかける
findings.governingReading: the breaker attached to his body threatens to trip
findings.explanation: A near-triggered bodily metaphor becomes a completed event and is given an explicit verbal message.

findings.highlight: I’ve had bruises pretty often
findings.evidenceJa: 生傷は絶えなかった
findings.governingReading: fresh injuries had never ceased
findings.explanation: Ongoing cuts and wounds become occasional bruising.

findings.highlight: That must be why I had such a dream
findings.evidenceJa: だからあんな夢を見たのかな
findings.governingReading: perhaps that is why he had such a dream
findings.explanation: A question-like hypothesis becomes certainty.

findings.highlight: This isn’t the time to worry about little things like being sick
findings.evidenceJa: 体がだるいとか腕に力が入らないとか言ってる場合じゃない
findings.governingReading: this is no time to talk about his sluggish body or lack of strength in his arms
findings.explanation: Specific alarming symptoms become “little things” and a generic illness.

findings.highlight: I hear Saber’s voice from the other side of the door
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=ふすま]襖ごしにセイバーの声がする
findings.governingReading: Saber’s voice comes through the fusuma partition
findings.explanation: The English again changes the house’s sliding partition into a door.

findings.highlight: I’ve recovered
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと熱は引きました
findings.governingReading: her fever has properly gone down
findings.explanation: A specific symptom resolution becomes recovery from the whole illness.

findings.highlight: It’s all thanks to your treatment
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩が看てくれたおかげ
findings.governingReading: thanks to Senpai watching over and caring for her
findings.explanation: Sakura’s gratitude for Shirou staying with her becomes gratitude for medical treatment.

findings.highlight: Stop making that face
findings.evidenceJa: すごく邪な感じがするんでやめてくれ
findings.governingReading: stop because that expression feels extremely improper or lewd
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s reason for objecting and the sexual coloring that launches Taiga’s joke.

findings.highlight: I just gave her some medicine yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日は熱計って薬出しただけ
findings.governingReading: yesterday he only took her temperature and gave her medicine
findings.explanation: mirror moon omits the temperature check from Shirou’s flustered defense.

findings.highlight: That’s offending as well
findings.evidenceJa: それはそれでムカツク
findings.governingReading: that irritates him in its own way
findings.explanation: The English uses the malformed expression “that’s offending.”

findings.highlight: smiles at me while making unreasonable demands
findings.evidenceJa: うんうん、と笑顔で無理難題を言いつける
findings.governingReading: Taiga nods cheerfully while imposing the impossible demand
findings.explanation: The English omits the self-satisfied nodding that carries the comic delivery.

findings.highlight: Sakura behind her, looking like she wants to say something
findings.evidenceJa: 何か言いたそうに俯いている桜
findings.governingReading: Sakura behind Taiga, looking down as though she wants to say something
findings.explanation: Sakura’s downcast posture, central to her hesitancy, disappears.

findings.highlight: Fuji-nee waves goodbye and leaves
findings.evidenceJa: 藤ねえは出勤していった
findings.governingReading: Taiga waves and leaves for work
findings.explanation: The English omits that Taiga departs for her job at school.

findings.highlight: I don’t have a bad cold
findings.evidenceJa: 熱はそう高くない
findings.governingReading: his fever is not especially high
findings.explanation: A measured symptom becomes a diagnosis of overall illness severity.

findings.highlight: Are you still a bit sick
findings.evidenceJa: 桜もまだ熱があるのか
findings.governingReading: does Sakura still have a fever
findings.explanation: Shirou asks about a specific continuing fever; the English generalizes it to mild illness.

findings.highlight: I take walks during the night
findings.evidenceJa: 最近は夜になると散歩してて
findings.governingReading: lately Shirou has been going for walks at night
findings.explanation: The English drops the recent onset that covertly refers to his Grail War patrols.

findings.highlight: It’ll be a huge help
findings.evidenceJa: 情けないんだが
findings.governingReading: shameful though it is for Shirou to ask
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou’s embarrassment about depending on Sakura.
